title: a union with a `Promise` constituent still carries a rejection channel, so `@throws {never}` on it is refused
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." `string | Promise<string>` is a shape the narrow lowering predicate answers 'no' for and that can still reject, so the trust question is asked through a deliberately wider predicate than the one that drives lowering. The control that localizes the extra `SMITHERS1508` is 09-foreign-calls/an-untrusted-union-return-is-an-executable-foreign-value-on-one-backend-only: it carries no marker at all and produces the same divergence, so the divergence belongs to the pre-existing union handling and not to the trust rule.

xfail.reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 through `run.mjs --backend go --json --filter union`, and the marker's previous sentence was WRONG in a way that would have misled whoever closed it. It said the fork reports [SMITHERS1301@5:23, SMITHERS1502@5:23]. It does not, and did not: the fork reports [SMITHERS1502@5:23] AND NOTHING ELSE. Confirmed against a pristine `git worktree` at HEAD as well as the working tree, so this is a stale note rather than a regression. So the fork omits TWO of the reference's three diagnostics, not one: the SMITHERS1508@6:10 for returning a value whose type has a foreign `Promise` constituent, AND the SMITHERS1301@5:23 must-use refusal at the same position as the SMITHERS1502 it does report. BOTH BACKENDS STILL REFUSE THE PROGRAM and both name SMITHERS1502 at the same position, so this remains a diagnostic-set divergence and not a soundness one — the refusal this case exists to pin is identical on both. The SMITHERS1508 half is PRE-EXISTING and belongs to `containsForeignExecutableValue`'s union handling, not to the `@throws {never}` trust rule: the sibling case an-untrusted-union-return-is-an-executable-foreign-value-on-one-backend-only carries no `@throws` marker anywhere and also loses the SMITHERS1508. The SMITHERS1301 half is NOT shared with that sibling — the sibling does not reach the must-use walk at all, because the fork stops it at a stock TS2322 — so the two no longer retire in one edit, and the earlier claim that they do was a consequence of the same mis-measurement. Two independent fork gaps are recorded here: the union arm of the executable-foreign-value rule, and a must-use refusal the fork does not raise on a trusted-marked union call.
